job.dataset: stable source catalogue identity; unchanged across ordinary INPX updates
job.plan: absolute path to an immutable native SQLite plan
job.output: absolute path to an empty folder or this dataset's existing compressed copy
job.seven_zip: absolute path to the installed, verified 7-Zip executable
job.jpeg_xl_encoder: absolute cjxl executable path, required by jpeg-xl-7z
job.jpeg_xl_decoder: absolute djxl executable path, required by jpeg-xl-7z

plan_schema: CREATE TABLE metadata(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,value TEXT NOT NULL)
INSERT INTO metadata VALUES('dataset',<same dataset as job>)

CREATE TABLE books(book_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,source TEXT NOT NULL,member TEXT NOT NULL,locator TEXT NOT NULL,filename TEXT NOT NULL,ext TEXT NOT NULL,inside_no INTEGER NOT NULL,fbd INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)

image_profiles.default: reversible-ppmd with original preserves all selected book bytes. Older markers without images mean original.
image_profiles.optional: illustrations-ppmd with balanced, economy or maximum applies HomeLibre Images to eligible FB2/EPUB without format conversion. illustrations-gray-ppmd also converts supported pictures to shades of gray. In maximum, eligible DjVu with a separate foreground mask can lose one background refinement when it reduces the ZIP member. Dimensions, other chunks and the size of the standalone DjVu stay unchanged. Requires the bookconvert scripts and HomeLibre Images in the installation tools folder. tools_root is optional and overrides that folder for an isolated runtime.
image_profiles.separated_jpeg: Catalogue mode jpeg-xl-7z with images=original uses upstream cjxl and djxl. It selects only JPEGs which get smaller and reconstruct byte for byte. The archive and any sidecar together must beat ordinary packing and the source archive. Reconstructed FB2 and EPUB may differ in container bytes. A PDF with packed JPEG streams is restored byte for byte. The original source files are untouched. The catalogue offers the independent encoder only when the profile is selected.
image_profiles.scope: Formats without an applicable transformation retain their book bytes. FLibrary companions and FBD containers retain the entire original package. FB2/EPUB over 64 MiB, DjVu over 128 MiB, unreadable books or format mismatches preserve their original bytes. Candidates must save space. The archive-level size safeguard can still keep the original archive.
image_profiles.continuation: The destination marker binds dataset, engine and image profile for all later runs. Changing profile requires a new output folder. Resume and INPX updates reuse verified archives while using the stored profile for new or changed sources.
image_profiles.counters: image_books_optimized and image_books_skipped count mapped locations for accepted transformed payloads and books individually declined by the processor, including reused locations. Opaque archives are counted separately. An already compact or unillustrated book is not counted as skipped.
image_profiles.availability: The catalogue command offers the three profiles for a new destination and reads the saved profile for continuation or INPX updates. It requests the optional image processor only for an explicit illustration profile.

mixed_zip: For selected formats with payloads from 16 KiB to 64 MiB the worker tries LZMA or PPMd. It falls back to ordinary Deflate or Copy if a candidate does not save at least 256 bytes and about one percent against the source ZIP member or loose file. This outer compression is lossless. The whole-archive size check still applies. LZMA and PPMd entries use the same optional 7-Zip decoder.

plan_contract.retained: Optional retained(book_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,folder TEXT,filename TEXT,ext TEXT,inside_no INTEGER,payload TEXT). The payload column is the relative physical archive path and should be indexed. Without the column, older plans use folder as the physical archive path. IDs must not overlap books. Reuse an already registered immutable payload without opening originals: its journal membership, every output artifact and companion image are checked first. Include every preserved target in the final location count.
plan_contract.book_id: Unique native plan-row ID, never a library LIBID. For ordinary rows it may equal the catalogue BookID. Native producer must retain a target map when including alternate CatalogBookCopies or personal-card locations; those targets need separate plan IDs. Original catalogue BookIDs must remain unchanged in the clone.
plan_contract.source: Canonical absolute physical archive or loose-file path. Resolve ZIP-to-7z fallback in the producer. The native caller enables allow_copy_inputs only when repacking into the same copy, to read newly downloaded or imported files. Managed archives, journals, catalogues and temporary areas remain excluded.
plan_contract.unavailable: Native only. Catalogue rows whose physical files are absent remain in the clone with their metadata and locators. A separate unavailable count excludes them from payload totals. A later pass looks first in the copy, then under the original root when the deferred locator still matches. A missing named member in a readable archive is also deferred. Inaccessible or damaged archives fail preparation.
plan_contract.member: Actual exact archive entry, or empty for a loose file. Native producer must reuse TMHLZip.ResolveBookName, including its existing safe legacy-index contract. Do not guess an unrelated member.
plan_contract.locator: Stable physical member identity within this source, independent of BookID and INPX row order.
plan_contract.filename: Original TBookRecord.FileName; retained only when copying an opaque original container.
plan_contract.ext: Original declared extension including the dot. No format conversion occurs.
plan_contract.inside_no: Original legacy archive index; retained only when copying an opaque original container.
plan_contract.fbd: Optional FBD-container locator flag, 0 if absent. A 1 keeps the whole original ZIP and its descriptor. The returned folder is the relative package directory including its trailing separator, and filename is the ZIP basename. Ordinary locators sharing the same physical ZIP keep the full ZIP path in folder.

output_contract.progress: UTF-8 JSON lines: source, books, compressing, verifying, prepared, canceled or error. Events carry sources_done/sources_total, books_done/books_total (plan locations), input_bytes/output_bytes for completed sources, reused and elapsed_seconds. current/total describe the current stage only; absence means indeterminate. Long operations send a heartbeat at least once per second while their bounded cancellation check runs. Fast member updates are throttled to 150ms, preserving first/final updates. UI ETA is explicitly approximate and is shown only after at least two completed sources and five seconds.
output_contract.prepared: generations/<generation>/prepared.json plus locations.sqlite; this is not a registered collection.
output_contract.locations_schema: locations(book_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,folder TEXT,filename TEXT,ext TEXT,inside_no INTEGER)
output_contract.folder: Relative to output. An ordinary locator points to a ZIP or 7z; an FBD locator points to the directory containing the named original ZIP. With keep_loose, when a separate file would grow in an archive, the original file is copied and its locator points to the containing directory with a trailing separator. Existing FLibrary containers retain their archive extension and side archives.
native_publication_required: Create consistent catalogue and personal-data snapshots without changing the source collection.
Remap every planned BookID in those snapshots using the returned locations. Preserve titles, authors, every series, source identities, groups, personal cards and reading state.
Include and remap alternate physical CatalogBookCopies and personal-card locations; do not leave their file pointers attached to the original library while claiming an independent copy.
Validate counts, the native database integrity, and actual book streams before registering the separate collection.
Use the final registered catalogue as the publication authority only after native validation and personal-data registration succeed atomically. Never expose a partial result.
Keep old referenced archive generations intact. Do not automatically delete source books or an older usable catalogue.
output_contract.sizes: input_bytes and output_bytes describe book/container payloads; catalogue, journal and scratch space must be displayed separately by the native UI. No guarantee of a compression ratio.
output_contract.cache: New ZIPs are extracted once and every member is checked against the prepared book SHA-256 before the payload is committed. Prepared bytes equal the original in reversible-ppmd. For modified books, the ledger records both original and prepared digests. Unchanged containers and companion files are compared byte for byte by SHA-256. On reuse, ordinary source checks use size and modification time; output checks also verify SHA-256 if modification time changed. Full verification of reused payloads reads every byte and must be an explicit slower option. Immutable payloads journal retains membership and artifact proofs for all completed package generations independently of the replaceable latest-source cache, including prepared but unapplied runs.

limits.large_loose_and_zip_originals: Loose originals stream in bounded chunks. A ZIP with oversized members is copied intact instead of being decoded and repacked.
limits.on_limit: Abort without publishing a collection; retain completed archives for resumption. Native acceptance against the real library is still required.

pending_engines: Public first-use download acceptance and incomplete companion checks for the separated JPEG writer
WebP image compression using upstream codecs; original LightLib Cleaner integration only if its callable interface and redistribution terms can be verified

exit_codes.0: Payloads prepared; native catalogue remapping and registration still required

archive_replacement_preparation.call: prepare_archive_replacement(source, replacements, workspace, seven_zip, method=None, canceled=...)
archive_replacement_preparation.inputs: One ZIP or 7z source, a mapping of exact member names to already transformed files, and an empty private workspace. No book-format conversion is performed by this primitive.
archive_replacement_preparation.source_preservation: 7-Zip -u- creates a separate candidate; the base archive and transformed input files remain untouched. Unselected members remain present with matching size and CRC; the candidate is fully tested by the codec. Selected members are additionally extracted and checked by SHA-256.
archive_replacement_preparation.metadata: ZIP comments are restored by rewriting central metadata only. Encoded filenames, UTF-8 flags and Unicode-path extras stay unchanged. ZIP64 size and locator offsets are updated. Duplicate/ambiguous logical names, unsafe replacement paths and encrypted entries are refused before any source mutation.
archive_replacement_preparation.no_growth: A candidate not smaller than the source is discarded and returns candidate=None. This does not alter the source.
archive_replacement_preparation.pending_commit: The caller must still exclusively revalidate the source identity, durably apply the verified result, refresh catalogue sizes and caches, preserve personal data, handle recovery, and provide the optional backup and UI workflow. PreparedArchive is never proof that a source was changed.
archive_replacement_preparation.verification: 10 real ZIP/solid-7z scenarios and 3 cleanup/ownership cases passed on Windows. Primary codec: 7-Zip 26.06 x64; additional full 13-case run: 7-Zip 26.05 x86 from the installed runtime, hosted by x64 Python. Synthetic inputs only; this is not an x86 catalogue workflow test.

native_replacement_commit.call: PrepareReplacement(source, candidate, expected_file_identity, source_sha256, result_sha256, compression_journal_root); BindContext(receipt_sha256); Execute; apply durable catalogue receipt; Acknowledge
native_replacement_commit.contract: Candidate format, selected members and neighboring contents must already be verified by the producer. Native preparation exclusively opens ordinary non-hardlinked files, validates source identity and both complete SHA-256 digests, and requires strict size reduction. Neither the source path nor its physical file identity changes.
native_replacement_commit.temporary_space: A prepared output file is still required. Its verified open handle is renamed into the compression journal on the same volume, not copied a second time. No complete original backup is made. The journal retains that output, small metadata and bounded pending-write blocks until catalogue acknowledgement.
native_replacement_commit.recovery: Schema 7 carries original-range and replacement-block digests plus the full final digest. Restart rejects changed completed blocks, changed not-yet-written original ranges, damaged pending/replacement data and foreign journals. RecoverReplacement and ordinary deletion Recover reject each other's journal kind. Compression cannot invoke whole-archive deletion.
native_replacement_commit.verification: 16 native scenarios passed independently on actual Win32 and Win64 executables. They include real ZIP and solid-7z candidates, preserved neighbors/comments, Unicode paths, strict no growth, no space, cancellation, hard links, external edits, nine actual process-termination boundaries, small results without an empty payload file and legacy ZIP deletion recovery. The bounded old/new footer comparison detects foreign bytes even after a partial footer write. The codec for producer checks was 7-Zip x64; the commit writers themselves ran in both architectures. Synthetic inputs only.
native_replacement_commit.pending_integration: Use a distinct compression journal root. The native BookCompressionJob now persists the matching catalogue receipt before mutation and can discover/recover an interrupted file/database operation. Selection adapters, application startup wiring, cache refresh, optional original-book backup and selection/profile/context-menu UI remain pending. No desktop installation or public release has been updated by these engine tests.

native_catalogue_receipt.call: TBookCompressionReceipt.Create(json); CheckBeforeWrite; bind SHA256 to PrepareReplacement; Execute file writer; Apply(writer); Acknowledge writer only after Apply succeeds
native_catalogue_receipt.schema: Schema 1, kind HomeLibre book compression. Top-level: collection_id; absolute catalogue/personal/source paths; catalogue_key/personal_key/source_file_key; source_sha256/result_sha256/profile_sha256; captured raw Bases.RootFolder and Bases.DBFileName values as base_root and base_catalogue; payloads and rows.
native_catalogue_receipt.payloads: Each exact member (empty for a loose file) has input_sha256, output_sha256 and size. No repeated members. Values are indexed once, including for many catalogue rows referring to one payload.
native_catalogue_receipt.rows: Each row has kind (0 catalogue Books, 1 personal Books, 2 CatalogBookCopies), id, lib_id, folder, file_name, ext, inside_no, old_size, root, source_key, member and required. Personal kind 1 is scoped by the receipt collection_id. Only personal mirrors may be optional; an unrelated historical card is preserved rather than overwritten. No duplicate target identities.
native_catalogue_receipt.guards: At most 16 MiB JSON and 100000 targets per physical-file receipt. Leases verify database file identities and prevent replacement while each connection is used. The captured Bases registration and exact row locator/LibID/size are rechecked. Missing databases are never created. The finished writer must match the receipt source path, physical identity, input/result hashes and immutable context digest.
native_catalogue_receipt.writes: Only BookSize in matching Books/CatalogBookCopies and the HomeLibreBookCompression ledger. IDs, source mappings, authors, series, genres, descriptions, notes, reviews, ratings, progress and other collections are unchanged. Both database writer locks are acquired before either set of rows changes; expensive file compression holds no database write transaction.
native_catalogue_receipt.replay: Catalogue and personal stores commit separately. The file journal must remain until both commits succeed. Old and already-applied new sizes are accepted on replay; a process crash between commits resumes idempotently. Failure before the first commit rolls back both stores. The ledger records per-member profile/input/output digests for the future incremental adapter; this component does not yet schedule recompression.
native_catalogue_receipt.verification: 15 native SQLite scenarios passed independently on Win32 and Win64: actual termination around file/catalogue/personal commits, rollback-journal and WAL replay, exact preservation of personal/related fields, 1000 catalogue aliases, late-created notes, changed rows or collection registration, replaced/missing databases, foreign receipts and a forced personal-write failure. Fixtures use synthetic databases and PNG-backed FB2 books. This is not the complete application workflow or a reopened Reader-position test.
native_catalogue_receipt.completion_check: CheckApplied reads both existing stores without writing. It requires applied sizes and the exact profile/input/output ledger. A completion marker alone cannot bypass an unfinished database commit.

native_compression_job.call: CreatePrepared(queue_root, receipt_json, candidate); Execute; refresh application caches; Forget. Restart: Pending(queue_root), OpenExisting(directory), Execute, then Forget after the caller refreshes.
native_compression_job.durability: Each compress-{GUID} job publishes an immutable receipt and its digest before the file engine starts. A unique child directory holds only compression recovery, separate from deletion. The existing native engine binds the receipt digest; one physical archive is finished before a caller advances to the next.
native_compression_job.replay: A process crash after journal publication resumes the file writer and both database commits. A durable completion marker bridges the gap before/after file-journal cleanup. Recovery checks the complete result digest, physical file identity and already-applied catalogue/personal sizes and ledger before accepting this marker. It does not reapply or replace personal text.
native_compression_job.preparation_boundary: The caller owns the already verified candidate and must prepare it on the same volume as the job queue. A crash before the file journal is published leaves the source unchanged; if its candidate is no longer present, the caller must reprepare from the verified unchanged source. This class does not recreate a missing candidate or resume an image codec.
native_compression_job.leases: A live job has an exclusive reader/writer lease plus a nonrenamable directory guard; the physical source uses the existing in-process writer guard and exclusive native file handles. Junction/reparse job directories are refused. Another native process cannot consume the same live receipt.
native_compression_job.cancellation: Cancellation is checked during preparation and immediately before file publication. Once writing starts, complete the current file safely. The operation owner must stop later jobs and decide whether an unstarted cancelled receipt should be resumed or discarded; application-level cancellation UI is still pending.
native_compression_job.cleanup: Forget is allowed only after a verified successful completion. It atomically moves the consumed job out of the pending namespace before removing fixed owned recovery filenames. Unknown files are preserved and reported; no recursive deletion or original-archive backup is performed. Cleanup does not reread a just-acknowledged multi-gigabyte archive solely to discard its receipt.
native_compression_job.pending_integration: Selected-book and all-alias capture, multi-file background operation, startup invocation, cache/Reader refresh, optional backup, format/profile preview and context-menu UI remain to be implemented and tested in the full application.
native_compression_job.verification: 11 native durable-job scenarios plus all 15 catalogue/personal receipt scenarios passed on each of Win32 and Win64 (26 cases per architecture, no skips). Actual process termination covered nine file/database/completion/cleanup boundaries. Checks include concurrent native consumers, premature completion, changed receipts, late personal notes, cancellation before write, unrelated queues, preservation of unknown files and readable Russian diagnostics. Synthetic books and lightweight real SQLite fixtures only; no complete catalogue UI or Reader reopen was exercised.

workspace_cleanup: Owned work directories validate canonical location and file identity before removal. Bounded retries handle transient Windows sharing errors after an external process exits; persistent failures remain errors. A replaced directory is preserved.
